Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The digital labour of artificial intelligence in Latin America: a comparison of Argentina, Brazil, and Venezuela (2502.06317v1) · paper method: Recorded worker interviews are transcribed, accompanied by debriefing reports and coded using both descriptive categories and literature-informed theoretical categories.

Permanent record ID: cohort8.claim.latinlabour.coding

  • Original author-stage note: Author-only candidate: separate source-verifier and adversarial source-content reviews remain pending.
  • Version-specific primary-source report. Proofs, model experiments, underlying data, consent/pay records and supplier participation have not been independently reproduced or audited.
  • Topics include task types, trajectories, informality and social protections; this methodology does not itself verify reported pay or any named supplier’s contribution.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The digital labour of artificial intelligence in Latin America: a comparison of Argentina, Brazil, and Venezuela (2502.06317v1) · paper method: Spanish-language questionnaires and interviews are fielded as paid platform tasks, with later follow-up and cross-platform re-fielding to examine pandemic-specific conditions.

Permanent record ID: cohort8.claim.latinlabour.paid-platform

  • Original author-stage note: Author-only candidate: separate source-verifier and adversarial source-content reviews remain pending.
  • Version-specific primary-source report. Proofs, model experiments, underlying data, consent/pay records and supplier participation have not been independently reproduced or audited.
  • Initial platform is Microworkers; original questionnaire is re-fielded through Clickworker in 2022. Participation is platform-mediated and not a random sample of all workers.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The digital labour of artificial intelligence in Latin America: a comparison of Argentina, Brazil, and Venezuela (2502.06317v1) · paper method: The authors state that statistical representativeness is difficult to apply because the boundaries and characteristics of platform populations are unknown.

Permanent record ID: cohort8.claim.latinlabour.representativeness

  • Original author-stage note: Author-only candidate: separate source-verifier and adversarial source-content reviews remain pending.
  • Version-specific primary-source report. Proofs, model experiments, underlying data, consent/pay records and supplier participation have not been independently reproduced or audited.
  • The study instead emphasizes comparable questionnaire/interface design, cross-platform variation and triangulation of worker interviews with survey responses.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The digital labour of artificial intelligence in Latin America: a comparison of Argentina, Brazil, and Venezuela (2502.06317v1) · paper method: The article combines a Spanish-language platform-worker study with a Portuguese-language Brazilian study, including questionnaires, follow-up interviews and online ethnography.

Permanent record ID: cohort8.claim.latinlabour.twin-studies

  • Original author-stage note: Author-only candidate: separate source-verifier and adversarial source-content reviews remain pending.
  • Version-specific primary-source report. Proofs, model experiments, underlying data, consent/pay records and supplier participation have not been independently reproduced or audited.
  • Argentina/Venezuela collection includes 2020–21 recruitment, 2022 follow-up and 2023 Argentine interviews; Brazilian study runs 2022–23. These are historical collection windows, not a 2026 census.
